title: The obligated verdict, written to the decision log, releasing the cell itself
action:
Add `bee cells dissent-verdict`, the orchestrator's obligated answer to a dissent (per 4b7aa303). Write it beside the record verb in `verbs/cells/dissent.rs`.

The verdict set is CLOSED and exhaustive: accept, reject, escalate. The reason is REQUIRED on all three — an answer with no reasoning is the decorative dissent this feature exists to prevent. Take them as plain flags, `--verdict accept|reject|escalate --reason "..."`, NOT as a `--file` payload: the `--file` plus versioned-schema pattern at `run_judge_record` exists because a judge verdict is foreign-model output, while a dissent verdict is session-authored. This is a deliberate, recorded deviation from that established pattern — write it in the cap report's deviations.

Three behaviors carry the locked requirements:

1. WRITE THE DECISION LOG. 4b7aa303 says the answer is recorded in the decision log before the related work resumes; a trace-only verdict does not satisfy it. `run_judge_record` shows the shape — it logs its own decision inside the same call, at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/handlers_meta.rs:169-311, near the end of the function.
2. FAIL CLOSED on that write. If the decision-log write fails, the dissent stays UNANSWERED — the trace is not stamped and the doors keep refusing. A half-answered dissent that clears a door is worse than no answer.
3. RELEASE THE CELL ITSELF. `run_reopen` at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs:1241 is the only unblock path today and it is claim-guarded, so shelling into it would trip on the very claim this feature releases elsewhere. Do the release inline, exactly as `run_judge_record` does its own reopen. All three verdict kinds release the block: 4b7aa303 obligates an ANSWER, and escalate-a-rung is one of the three answers.

The verdict verb takes NO worker-shaped claim-ownership guard. It is the orchestrator's verb by 4b7aa303, and a guard modeled on `guard_claim_ownership` (packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/trace.rs:205) would make `--force-ownership` the routine path for an audited override. Record that reasoning in the module.

Declare the verb in the same five places sd-1 declared its own: the cells dispatch table at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/util.rs:68, the router coverage line at packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/router.rs:71 (currently `    "cells judge|judge-record|reset-budget|schedule|archive|unarchive",`), `src/generated/registry_payload.json` by hand, and the flag ratchet in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/catalog.rs for any genuinely new flag name.

truths: A verdict of accept, reject, or escalate with a reason appends to the dissent record and appears in the decision log.
A verdict outside the closed set, or one with no reason, refuses by name and writes nothing.
After any of the three verdicts, a cell blocked by a blocker dissent is released and its dependents are schedulable again.
A verdict recorded when no dissent exists refuses by name.
A second verdict on an already-answered dissent refuses by name.
When the decision-log write fails, the dissent stays unanswered and the trace is not stamped.
The orchestrator records a verdict on a cell a worker recorded against without needing an ownership override.
artifacts: The verdict verb and its tests in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/cells/dissent.rs
key_links: The verdict verb is reachable through the cells dispatch table and declared in the registry payload.
The release is written inline in this verb, not delegated to run_reopen.
prohibitions: run_reopen is not called from this path and its own behavior is unchanged.
No versioned JSON schema module is introduced for this payload.
A failed decision-log write never leaves a stamped trace.
